correctness.rationale: For the printed polynomial flow the Jacobian trace is exactly \(-\sigma-1-5b-d\). Jacobi's determinant identity yields \(\det D\phi_T=\exp[-(\sigma+1+5b+d)T]\), and the product of the five tangent singular values equals the determinant magnitude. Thus every standard full finite-time Lyapunov spectrum sums exactly to that constant, and any full asymptotic spectrum has the same sum. Exact rational arithmetic gives \(-92/3\) at the source parameters, versus the printed sums \(-16447/5000\) and \(-71247/5000\). The proof uses no finite experiment to infer an infinite-time statement; the asymptotic statement is a direct limit of an exact finite-time identity.

value.rationale: Figure 2's five Lyapunov exponents are a central quantitative diagnostic used by the primary article to distinguish its \(r=43\) chaotic example from its \(r=25\) non-chaotic example. The exact phase-volume law is trajectory-independent and exposes order-one discrepancies of about 27.38 and 16.42 in the sums, far beyond rounding. Correct full spectra are necessary for reproducible dynamical classification and any downstream use of contraction rates or Lyapunov-derived dimensions. The result is therefore a substantive source-specific consistency correction, while carefully preserving the possibility that the qualitative regimes survive a corrected computation.
